pr_title: kubelet: dockershim ExecSync should return context.DeadlineExeceeded on timeout
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: Andrew Sy Kim <kim.andrewsy@gmail.com>

**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/94115 we fixed a bug where kubelet did not respect exec probe timeouts. That PR also re-enabled some tests to ensure we don't regress. So far all the tests using containerd have been passing, but some tests using dockershim started to fail (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/96463). This wasn't caught during presubmit since jobs that run dockershim only run e2es marked with `[NodeConformance]`. 

The bug is in the CRI implementation of dockershim where it should be returning `context.Deadline` in the ExecSync response instead of `exec.TimedoutError`. `TimedoutError` is actually the error as expected by the prober, which is what should be returned by the gRPC client, not the server. The server is expected to return `context.DeadlineExeceeded`, which results in the cri client returning `TimedoutError` back to the prober. 

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/96463

review_comments:
remote_runtime.go expects a grpc error with status code `DeadlineExceeded` if exec timed out:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4bb30c3b0e9167eb85b1e3b0c9a3bab3b351a3e2/pkg/kubelet/cri/remote/remote_runtime.go#L394-L397
maybe this comment can be added into the code. It is not very logical when you simply looking at this method
nothing bad will happen, but maybe need to call `cancel()`?
cancel is called with defer on line 112
yes, totally. My comment is that we can cancel timeout in case the exec has already finished =)

This test started to flake once dockershim was updated to correctly return DeadlineExceeded grpc status error. It seems like the default 1s timeout was  too aggressive here, my guess is because `pull-kubernetes-e2e-node` is probably very resource starved. I updated this to 5 seconds and the test seems to be passing consistently. 

Increasing the timeout here seems safe, because this test is really expecting that the exit code from the probe returns 0, it should allow for the probe to take longer than the default 1s, as long as it doesn't return a non-zero exit code.
should the same be on line 124?

hmmm.. so that test wasn't failing because the test is expecting a restart, but now that you mention it may be failing due to timeout and not a non-zero exit code, so I think it may make sense to set a similar timeout there.
This timeout check was incorrect because `StartExec` is a blocking call.
